newsitem.title: JAPAN: Current yen rate won't affect Japan car trade - JAMA.
newsitem.headline: Current yen rate won't affect Japan car trade - JAMA.

text.p: The current yen/dollar rate is not expected to affect exports by Japanese carmakers, Hiroshi Okuda, a vice chairman of the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association (JAMA), told reporters on Thursday.
"The current 116 to 117 (yen per dollar rate) is an appropriate level," said Okuda, who is also president of Toyota Motor Corp.
Japanese business lobby Keidanren and JAMA have previously said that a yen/dollar rate of 110 to 120 was an appropriate level, "so the current yen/dollar rate is not a problem," he added.
"We would like to avoid sharp fluctuations in the currency rate, if possible, because they make it hard for companies to set a business plan," he said.
Nobuhiko Kawamoto, president of Honda Motor Co and also a JAMA vice chairman, echoed Okuda's views.
"We hope the yen/dollar rate will stabilise at 110 to 120 and we must watch currency rates on a long-term basis," he said.
"Honda does not rely on forward foreign exchange contracts substantially, so the strengthening of the yen will not affect our company's business," he added.
